title: Setting your hourly rate and minimum charge for carpet and upholstery cleaning
audience: Owners of carpet and upholstery cleaning businesses who need a base hourly rate and a per-room or per-item check before they quote.
learningOutcomes: Separate billable hours from non-billable hours, and calculate the time available to bill.
Calculate a base hourly rate from the owner's own costs and income target, then compare it with local evidence.
Set a minimum charge for short jobs, and explain it to a client before the visit.

instruction.heading: What moves the rate for carpet and upholstery work
instruction.body: The rate depends on the operator's skill, the equipment used, how much soiling or staining the work involves, the range of services offered in one visit (carpets, upholstery, rugs and drapes) and the cost of running the business. Carpet work is usually priced per room or per item, so the hourly rate is a tool for building those prices. The research did not find an Australian hourly rate for carpet cleaning. The directory figures are per room and per item (Yellow Pages, 9 January 2025).

instruction.heading: Counting the hours that can be billed
instruction.body: Paid hours include travel, quoting and site visits, admin, marketing, training, equipment servicing, sick days and leave. Jobber's general guide puts billable time at about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours. That is not an Australian figure, so check your own log against it. If you can bill 60 of every 100 paid hours, the costs of all 100 must come from the 60, so the rate is about 1.67 times the rate for a fully billable week (CALC).

instruction.heading: Building the rate from costs and income
instruction.body: Add the annual running costs (equipment and its servicing, vehicle, solution, water and waste, insurance, phone, software, marketing and accounting) to the income you need, including leave and super where you pay wages. Business.gov.au says on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure (1 October 2026). Divide the total by billable hours. Business Victoria advises including total overheads and reviewing prices about every three months (no date shown).

instruction.heading: Test the rate against a room and an item
instruction.body: Convert the rate into time per room and per item. At an illustrative $50 an hour, a room that takes 30 minutes earns $25, which is the bottom of the directory's per-room steam range of $25 to $45 (CALC on Yellow Pages). A directory average of $55 per room pays for about 66 minutes at $50 an hour (CALC). If a room takes less time than that, check your prices and your times before you accept the job.

instruction.heading: Set a minimum charge for small jobs
instruction.body: A single chair or a small rug still needs travel, set-up and pack-down. Contractor+ suggests setting a minimum from the full visit cost, divided by one minus the target margin, with the minimum covering travel, set-up and cleanup. Its figures are illustrative. Gap: the research did not find a carpet minimum charge. State your minimum in writing before the visit.

procedure: Estimate paid working hours in a year, then subtract travel, visits, admin, marketing, training and leave to find billable hours.
List the annual running costs, including equipment, vehicle, solution, water, waste, insurance, phone, software and marketing.
Add the income needed, with leave and tax allowances confirmed by a registered tax agent.
Divide the total by billable hours to find the base rate.
Convert the rate into time per room and per item, and check each price against that time.
Set and state a minimum for small jobs, and review the rate each quarter.

workedExamples.situation: [ILLUSTRATIVE] A solo carpet cleaner plans for about 1,800 paid hours a year and expects to bill 60 per cent of them. Annual costs and the income needed total $54,000 (illustrative). A visit to a single chair or rug costs about $45 in travel and time (illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What base rate is needed, what does a 30-minute room earn at that rate, and what minimum should a small job carry?
workedExamples.reasoning: Billable hours are 1,800 x 0.60, which is 1,080 (CALC). The base rate is $54,000 divided by 1,080, which is $50.00 an hour. A 30-minute room earns $25.00 at that rate (CALC), which is the bottom of the directory's per-room steam range (Yellow Pages). A directory average of $55 per room pays for about 66 minutes at $50 an hour (CALC), so the cleaner checks how long a room really takes. The minimum for a small visit follows the Contractor+ method: $45 divided by 0.70 is $64.29 at a 30 per cent target margin (illustrative figures).

commonErrors.error: Setting prices from the lowest directory offer.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the rate from your costs and billable hours. Compare with the directory and note the source.

commonErrors.error: Pricing as though every paid hour could be billed.
commonErrors.prevention: Subtract travel, visits, admin, marketing and leave before dividing.

commonErrors.error: Pricing by the room without checking the minutes a room takes.
commonErrors.prevention: Time your rooms, and check the price against that time.

commonErrors.error: Taking single chairs or rugs with no minimum.
commonErrors.prevention: Set and state a minimum that covers travel, set-up and pack-down.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Price display: show the total including GST (business.gov.au, 18 January 2024). The research did not confirm the rules for minimum or call-out charges, so check current ACCC guidance before publishing one.

Where you employ cleaners, the Cleaning Services Award may set their pay: Level 1 adult minimum of $25.85 an hour with 25 per cent casual loading from 1 July 2025 (Fair Work Commission). The 2026-27 rates were not checked.
Tax treatment of leave and super for a sole trader was not confirmed. Check it with a registered tax agent before publishing a rate.
This lesson does not grant a licence or insurance. Licence rules for carpet and upholstery cleaning were not researched, so check the rules for your state or territory.

qualityStandard: Billable hours are calculated from a logged or estimated month, not assumed.
The base rate is built from the owner's costs and income target, and is compared with local evidence.
A minimum charge is set and stated before any short job.
documentationEvidence: Annual costs and income worksheet, with the source and date of each cost
Billable hours calculation showing the non-billable deductions
Price sheet showing the base rate, the minimum charge and the review date
summary: Build the rate from billable hours, then test it against the time each room and item takes.
Directory prices are references. They show the range of what is advertised, not your costs.
Gaps: no Australian carpet hourly rate, minimum charge or wastewater cost was found in the research.

knowledgeChecks.question: A carpet cleaner can bill 60 of every 100 paid hours. How should the rate be built?
options: From all paid hours, so the rate looks lower
From billable hours, so costs and income come from the work that can be billed
From the lowest directory offer in the area
From the rate the owner wishes the market would pay

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a single chair or rug have a minimum charge?
options: Travel, set-up and pack-down do not shrink with a small job
Clients expect every job to cost the same
A minimum replaces a written quote
Small items need no set-up time at all

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best way to check a per-room price?
options: Compare the price with the minutes the room takes at your billable rate
Use the lowest offer you can find
Ask a friend what they charge

sourceReferences: business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. Supports: on-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Jobber Academy, 'What are billable hours', https://getjobber.com/academy/what-are-billable-hours/, published 5 November 2024, last modified 20 July 2026. Supports: billable time is about 60 to 80 per cent of working hours; a general range, not an Australian figure.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Victoria. Supports: include total overheads and sales costs in the price; review prices about every three months.

Yellow Pages Australia, 'Carpet cleaning costs', https://www.yellowpages.com.au/articles/home-cleaning/carpet-cleaning-costs, published 9 January 2025, updated November 2025. Vendor directory. Supports: per-room, whole-home and upholstery price ranges, and a warning that offers as low as $10 a room may be a basic one-step process.

Contractor+, 'Minimum Service Call Charge: A Contractor's Pricing Guide', https://contractorplus.app/blog/minimum-service-call-charge, 23 September 2026. Supports: a minimum can be set from the full visit cost divided by one minus the target margin, and should cover travel, set-up and cleanup. The page labels its figures illustrative; none are used here.

Fair Work Commission, Cleaning Services Award (MA000022), https://awards.fairwork.gov.au/MA000022.html, variation effective 1 July 2025. Supports: Level 1 adult minimum hourly rate of $25.85 and a 25 per cent casual loading. The 1 July 2026 position was not checked.
business.gov.au, 'Display prices', https://business.gov.au/legal/fair-trading/display-prices, page metadata 18 January 2024. Supports: displayed prices should show the total price, including GST.

Notes: 1,800 paid hours, the $54,000 target, the $45 visit cost and the 30 per cent margin are illustrative. The $50 an hour is the result of the illustrative inputs. The directory figures are vendor data.
